official_finding.summary: SkyTruth Cerulean's detector logged a 19.63 km, 3.85 km² slick on this scene (model confidence 0.929). A Cerulean human reviewer classed it 'Vessel, coincident', their strongest class, and Cerulean's own record names MMSI 212656000 as the vessel, one of three its scorer considered (best collated source score 0.4887). That MMSI does not appear anywhere in our own scene-time AIS extract for this case. Independent cross-referencing of its IMO (9730335) against VesselTracker, VesselFinder and MarineTraffic (2026-09-12) found the same hull currently broadcasting as MMSI 636016487, name HORIZON — present in our AIS extract and UDGAM's own top-scored suspect.

MID 636 indicates Liberia; the Cyprus flag given in the cross-check notes belongs to the old MMSI's MID (212) and is not asserted for this one.

official_finding.caveat: Another algorithm's output with analyst review, not an investigation: Cerulean attributed the slick to MMSI 212656000, and nothing here establishes responsibility. Two co-candidate MMSIs were also scored (248264000, 210007000). The scene carries other Cerulean slicks that are not this case — 3687317 at 126 km and 3687321 at 76 km, attributed elsewhere, plus two on the adjacent frame; ours is the 19.6 km one. No volume was reported. MMSI 212656000 does not appear in our own scene-time AIS extract; an independent IMO cross-check (9730335, 2026-09-12) found the same hull currently broadcasting as MMSI 636016487 (HORIZON), which does appear in our feed and is UDGAM's own top-scored suspect. That cross-check's stated flag (Cyprus) does not match MMSI 636016487's MID (636, which indicates Liberia) — the Cyprus/MID-212 justification in the source note describes the old MMSI, not this one, so the flag is not asserted here. Treat the HORIZON identity as provisional until the MID/flag discrepancy is resolved.

assessment.explanation: A hit, once the corrected identity is used: HORIZON (636016487) — the MMSI an independent IMO cross-check resolved as the same hull Cerulean's record names — is UDGAM's own top-ranked suspect, scored 0.620, closest approach 2.34 km from the origin peak (against r90 8.82 km) at grid probability 0.844. It is the clear top score: the next two scored candidates trail at 0.345 and 0.046. Our funnel 6 → 4 → 3 → 3 named this vessel first, and it is the one the corrected record points to. Two things this does not resolve, the same as Jacksonville: Cerulean's own record still lists a different MMSI (212656000) that never appears in our AIS feed under that number — either Cerulean's registry and our live scene-time AIS disagree about this hull's MMSI, or these are two vessels sharing an IMO for reasons not independently confirmed beyond the tracker cross-check. And the flag stated for HORIZON in the cross-check notes (Cyprus) does not match its MID (636, Liberia), which needs resolving before this goes in front of a judge as verified.
assessment.what_would_have_helped: Nothing about the physics changed — the origin cloud and funnel were already landing the right vessel at #1 once matched to the right MMSI. What would have helped is exactly what surfaced this correction: cross-referencing IMO against multiple trackers rather than trusting Cerulean's registry MMSI at face value, since the earlier 'miss' verdict rested entirely on comparing against an MMSI (212656000) that turns out not to be the one this hull was broadcasting under. Making that cross-check step routine — or resolving the flag/MID mismatch it introduced here — is now the harder half of the work.
